notes: No release before 0.5.0 may claim any of this is balanced: every magnitude in the shipped content carries tuningStatus untuned and the balance harness owns all of them -- so this file is a measurement and not a balance claim.

The universe is still degenerate in the following ways, and this edit closes two of them and withdraws two statements the superseded files made. The fast and horizon sweeps are 100 percent passive-control and submit no god verb; the ascension sweep round-robins all eight strategies, which is the one place a strategy is exercised at all, and the superseded files called all three passive. Scribing no longer stops for good when the stock empties: the single materials pool is now food, stone and vellum and a scribe spends only vellum, so over the reference two hundred years the final twenty-year window scribes 5 books where it used to scribe none. Portals now open. The superseded files say nothing in packages/scenario opens one and that no raid runs in any committed sweep, and that is no longer true: raids.ts installs the arrival process and drives rules-raid to termination, and the executor declares raidEngagement true by default. Teaching does not die out either -- but the superseded files' statement that a lesson is taught in every one of the ten twenty-year windows, the thinnest holding 16, is withdrawn as false. It held for one run seed. Three of five seeds violate it on the tree those files were measured on, and three of five violate it here. Teaching supply oscillates and a two-hundred-year horizon can end inside a trough; packages/scenario/test/unit/reference-long-run.test.ts carries the seeds, the per-window supply counts and the three explanations they rule out.
rationale: The economy wire arriving in the gate sweeps, regenerated once from the merged tree. The merge took main's three baselines as an explicit placeholder rather than hand-merging this branch's against them, so every delta recorded here is this tree against main at f97cc76 -- a comparison somebody can reproduce -- and not against an intermediate nobody ran. The content set changed and the digest says so, 6b18886a -> ba7be8d6: fourteen form.json records gained yieldWeights, five territory.json records gained yieldPerLandUnit, seven raid constants that make a raid fire were added, and main's max-summons-per-side edit from 16 to 8 came across. Two things changed at once and the split between them is not measured here: the economy wire, and raids firing in a committed sweep for the first time -- main's executor declares raidEngagement false because nothing there opens a portal, and this tree's declares it true. Attributing the movements below to one or the other wants the A/B the executor already carries, a run built with raids false, and that is a measurement rather than a merge. No tolerance was widened, and no constant, cap or magnitude was tuned to produce any movement below. At two hundred world years the wire is not a small effect and this file is where it shows. Every metric rises and the largest is referenceLivingMages, 69.5 -> 459.875 (390.375, 100.72 SE) -- a mage population six and a half times the one main measures. referencePopulation and referencePopulationChange each rise 9763.125 (7.67 SE) to 15732.25, referencePeakPopulation 19381 -> 29490 (10109, 19.73 SE), referenceGrimoires 105.75 -> 283.5625 (177.8125, 4.29 SE), referenceKnowledgeInstances 2035.25 -> 3266.59375 (1231.34375, 3.82 SE) and referenceLibraryDepth 24.9375 -> 34.125 (9.1875, 2.70 SE). The reason the ascension gate exists is visible in the three files read together: the same change is worth -1.39 SE of books at five years, -4.23 SE at twenty, and +4.29 SE at two hundred. Two mechanisms arrive together and this file cannot separate them: construction had no caller before this branch, so no university was ever finished and no capacity was ever added, and raids did not fire in a committed sweep at all. Both compound over two centuries and neither is isolated here. What did not compound is knowledge. referenceNodesKnown 58.125 -> 60.875 and referenceNodesGained 55.625 -> 58.375 are 0.25 SE, and referenceNodesGainedFinalQuarter 3.75 -> 4.875 is 0.66 SE. The wire changes how much a universe has, not how much it knows -- what it knows is still held down by the content ceiling, and that is the same finding the horizon file records from the other side.
